reason: briefcase bundle entry — MUST import cli post-sys.path-swap. The launcher first runs prepare() (briefcase-bundled), then evicts kohakuterrarium.* from sys.modules and prepends the active version tree to sys.path. Importing cli at module top would pin it to the briefcase-bundled framework (defeating the in-process version swap that makes self-update work on briefcase shells where _pth disables PYTHONPATH).

Lazy import of the DriveScreen panel. It transitively imports terrarium.* and studio, whose package __init__ pulls builtins.outputs -> tui.output -> tui.session; a module-top import would be a runtime import cycle (CULL_KEEP partial-init) since tui.app is imported during tui.session init. The TerrariumService is injected duck-typed onto TUISession by the engine_cli runner, so this lazy widget import is the only remaining terrarium-reaching seam. Matched by function+target (not line) so unrelated edits do not re-break the gate.

test-only seam guarded by KT_TEST_LLM_SCRIPT env var; production runs never import the testing package (its __init__ eagerly loads the whole test harness). A fresh subprocess has no injection point, so an env-guarded lazy import is the only mechanism. Matched by function+target (not line) so unrelated edits do not re-break the gate.

Lazy import of api.app.create_app — the Android launcher loads via JNI before the framework's heavy api/serving graph needs to be in memory.  Lazy import means an import-time failure surfaces in the foreground-service log (visible via adb logcat) instead of silently killing the Python interpreter at module load.
Lazy import of serving.web.start_uvicorn_with_port_fallback — paired with the create_app lazy import above; both share the same JNI-cold-start rationale.
